findings.description: This subnet automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses and is associated with a route table that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to an Internet Gateway. Workloads placed here can be directly Internet reachable when their security groups permit it.

This subnet automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses and is associated with an Internet-routable route table. The portal instance is deployed here, and its attached security group permits Internet ingress.
The EBS volume does not explicitly enable encryption or specify a KMS key. Encryption therefore depends on an account-level default that is not established by this configuration.

The user-data script embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. These long-lived credentials can be exposed through source control, Terraform-managed artifacts, user-data access, or compromise of the instance.
TCP/22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0. This group is attached to an instance in a public, Internet-routable subnet, exposing SSH to arbitrary Internet hosts.
TCP/80 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0 to the publicly addressed portal instance, exposing its Apache service directly to all Internet hosts without a configured access boundary.
All protocols and ports are permitted to 0.0.0.0/0. The publicly reachable instance has no egress restriction, enabling unrestricted outbound connectivity if it is compromised.

The bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no bucket-level server-side encryption configuration. Encryption at rest for potentially sensitive network telemetry is therefore not enforced by this configuration.
The snapshot is created from an EBS volume that is not configured as encrypted. It can consequently preserve disk data without encryption at rest.
